body:
Review findings addressed in e8d8069 (quick gate green: motion 161 s, app 336 s, ui 337 s, 0 failed):
1. **Moved work offset (blocking)**: `posting::program_ops` re-runs the spindle law for turning ops and the lathe Drill against the live work-offset origin and refuses by name; `current_stamp` also carries the selected slot's origin (written only when not the world origin, so no existing stamp changes) - moving G54 after generation stales the op. The review's exact scenario (Facing, then G54 to (0,1,0)) is refused naming F1, 1.000 mm, G54.
2. **Lean x radius (blocking)**: the law reads every vertex's radius/height about the fitted axis and about world Z through the origin; the worst disagreement must be within 0.0005 mm. A 30 mm x 0.4 mm washer leaning 2 mrad (old law: 0.4 um) is refused - its face would post as a 30 um cone. Boundary cases at 0.98x / 1.02x pass / refuse.
3. **Fit noise (should-fix, real)**: an STL-like plumb revolve (uneven segments, seam sliver, f32 vertices) fitted 1.1 um off (2.2x the tolerance) - a false refusal. New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/axis_refine.rs` refines the fitted direction from the facets' normal-line concurrency (Plucker coordinates, Gauss-Newton), kept only if it moves > 1e-12 rad and doesn't worsen the residual (evenly tessellated parts keep their exact old fit). Worst case now 3.3e-6 mm (~150x under).
4. Tests: Y-offset turning case, a G55 height reference, a second setup's own G54.
5. Wording: "within one last digit".
Because the shared fit changed, rotary_verify / rotary_letter / rotary_fixtures / rotary_field_parity and the motion rotary suites were also run - green. Lathe goldens byte-identical.

Independent re-review: no blocking findings - all five fixes close their holes (post-time re-check covers every route to G-code; return to the world origin is caught; the refinement only replaces the eigen fit when it doesn't worsen the residual). Should-fix items (off-centre features bias the fit and the refusal's advice can't fix it; a keyed-revolve guard test) are filed as #71. Merging as the first PR of the 0.12.0 cut.
